verses.text: Brothers and sisters, we want you to know about the grace God has given the churches in Macedonia.
Even in a severe time of testing and deep poverty, they overflowed with joy and became remarkably generous.
I can confirm that they gave as much as they could—and even beyond what they could afford—entirely on their own.
They urgently begged us for the privilege of sharing in this service for God's people.
They did more than we expected: first they gave themselves to the Lord, and then, by God's will, they gave themselves to us too.
So we urged Titus, who had already started this work, to help you finish this act of grace as well.
Just as you excel in everything—in faith, speech, knowledge, eagerness, and love for us—excel in this grace of giving too.
I'm not commanding you to give. I'm showing you how eager others are, to test whether your love is genuine too.
You know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ: though he was rich, he became poor for your sake, so that through his poverty you could become rich.
Here's my advice: last year you were the first not only to act but also to want to do this.
So now finish what you started. Let your eagerness to do it be matched by completing it with what you have.
If you're eager to give, your gift is accepted according to what you have, not according to what you don't have.
We don't want others to have it easy while you are crushed.
We want fairness. Right now your surplus can meet their need, and later their surplus can meet yours. That's how fairness works.
As Scripture says, ‘The one who gathered a lot had nothing left over, and the one who gathered a little had no shortage.’
Thanks be to God, who put the same deep concern for you into Titus' heart.
He welcomed our appeal and was already so eager that he chose to come to you on his own.
We're sending along with him a brother whose work for the Good News is praised by all the churches.
The churches also appointed him to travel with us as we carry this gift, a service that honors the Lord and shows our eagerness to help.
We want to avoid any criticism about how we handle this generous gift.
We're taking care to do what is honorable, not only before the Lord but also before people.
We're also sending another brother who has often proved eager in many things. Now he is even more eager because he has great confidence in you.
As for Titus, he is my partner and co-worker in serving you. As for our brothers, they are representatives of the churches and bring honor to Christ.
So show these brothers proof of your love, and show the churches why we have been proud of you.
